title: From Prototype to Production Agents

sections.heading: Everyday Analogy
sections.body:
Think of a restaurant kitchen.

One cook alone can make a simple dish. But for a big wedding, you need many cooks with different jobs, a recipe chart on the wall, and a head chef who decides who does what next.

ADK is that kitchen system for AI. An agent is a helper that can think with an LLM. Multi-agent orchestration means many helpers work together. A graph-based workflow is the recipe chart showing clear paths from start to finish.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body:
Normal agents are prototypes. They work for demos but fail at enterprise scale.

Google's ADK exists to build production agents. It weaves two things:
- Deterministic logic means fixed code that always does the same steps. Predictable.
- LLM reasoning means flexible AI thinking that adapts to new words.

It also adds structured context management, which means giving each agent only the right memory it needs, and model-agnostic deployment, which means you can run the same system with different AI models and languages like Python or Java.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body:
Without clear graphs, agents get confused about who does what. Work loops or stops.

Without structured context, agents get too much memory and forget what matters, or share private data.

Without hybrid logic, pure AI can be unreliable for payments or safety steps that need exact rules.

ADK fixes this with explicit execution paths, efficient context, and evaluation for reliability and throughput.

steps.narration: A user asks for something complex, like booking a trip.
The graph, your recipe chart, picks the explicit path to follow.
Specialist agents handle parts, mixing fixed code and AI thinking.
Context manager gives each agent only the memory it needs.
The system runs reliably with any model or language at scale.

quiz.q: What is multi-agent orchestration in simple words?
options: Many specialist agents working together with a clear plan
Only fixed code with no AI
quiz.why: ADK is for multi-agent systems where agents are orchestrated via graphs to handle complex tasks together.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x without ADK's production features?
options: Agents lose track of context, paths break, and throughput drops
quiz.why: Without graph-based paths and efficient context management, reliability and throughput fail at scale.

quiz.q: What does hybrid deterministic and AI reasoning mean?
options: Weaving predictable fixed code with flexible LLM thinking
Using only one AI model forever
quiz.why: ADK weaves deterministic code for predictable outcomes with adaptive AI reasoning.

extra: ADK 2.0 supports Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, and Kotlin and includes Agents CLI for scaffold, test, and deploy.
